title: Lab 2: Analog RC Low-Pass Filter & Bode Plot
author: Bioelectrical Lab Sim Demo
description: Design and characterize a first-order RC low-pass filter (fc ≈ 1.59 kHz) on the NI ELVIS II prototyping board using the Function Generator, Oscilloscope, and Bode Analyzer.

steps.title: Build a 1.59 kHz RC Low-Pass Filter on ELVIS II
steps.instruction: With ELVIS II mode ON, wire FGEN (Row 33) through a 1 kΩ resistor to your output node, and connect a 100 nF capacitor from the output node to GROUND (Row 49 or 53). Wire AI 0+ to FGEN, AI 1+ to the filter output, and AI 0− / AI 1− to AIGND.
steps.hint: Check fc = 1 / (2π × 1 kΩ × 100 nF) = 1.592 kHz using the topbar RC Calc tool!

checks.label: NI ELVIS II mode is active

steps.title: Measure −3 dB Cutoff on the Bode Analyzer
steps.instruction: Open the Bode Analyzer (right rail), ensure Stimulus is FGEN and Response is AI 1 (or your output probe), and verify the measured −3 dB cutoff frequency is near 1.59 kHz.
steps.hint: In Full Bench Bode view you can drag the frequency cursor directly to 1.59 kHz and observe −3.0 dB gain and −45° phase shift.

checks.label: Measured −3 dB cutoff fc ≈ 1.59 kHz (±250 Hz)

steps.title: Verify Time-Domain Attenuation on the Oscilloscope
steps.instruction: Open FGEN (set 4 Vpp Sine at 1592 Hz and press Run) and view CH 0 (input) and CH 1 (filtered output) on the Oscilloscope.
steps.hint: At f = fc, a 4.0 Vpp input attenuates by 0.707× to ~2.83 Vpp with a 45° phase lag.

checks.label: CH 1 filtered output reads ~2.83 Vpp (±0.4 V)

steps.title: Compare 100 nF vs 1 µF Cutoff
steps.instruction: Try swapping the 100 nF capacitor for the 1 µF capacitor and observe how the cutoff shifts down by 10× (to ~159 Hz), then check off below.
steps.hint: Doubling or multiplying C by 10 divides fc by the same factor because fc = 1 / (2πRC).

checks.label: I verified the 10× shift in cutoff frequency when changing C
